audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in the Kirton 1967 PDF we hold at pp. 25-26 ( lines 499-522), as the record's the domain locator states. (2) Deciding source: a 1967 phonology article by the language's long-term SIL describer; impressionistic but first-hand, and it remains the only stress description. The held 1996 reference grammar (C-131) defers to it and independently restates the non-final-stress rule (p. 193 n.2); the held 1978 consonant paper uses penultimate-stress retention as a syllable diagnostic (p. 182), again consistent. The 1992 Bradley & Kirton dictionary sketch, downloaded now (57 MB scan, scanned of the sound-system pages), is silent. No JIPA illustration, dissertation, or instrumental study of Yanyuwa prosody was found. (3) list of works to obtain: one low-priority print-only item (2016/17 encyclopaedia vol. 2 sounds chapter). (4) Coding: 'fixed-strict' with initial+penultimate patt
